# A5K

> An open, Amiga-inspired deterministic display and audio card for PCIe. Not an
> Amiga, not a clone, no 68k or Kickstart compatibility. Specified from the
> Copper up; no hardware has been built.

## Canonical facts

- **Project:** A5K — An Amiga-Inspired Deterministic Display and Audio Card.
- **Author:** Ryan David Hall (AKA "ProphetPX"). One-person design study.
- **Current revision:** Rev. AW (B49), 4 November 2026; documentation through
  10 November 2026. The revision is a documentation label, not a hardware release.
- **Status:** design study. No RTL, no PCB, no prototype, no measurement.
- **What it is:** a specification for a PCIe add-in card that generates display
  and audio with a published, slot-exact timing contract — a Copper-style
  sequencer, planar scanout, a minterm blitter and deterministic audio.
- **What it is not:** an Amiga, an Amiga clone, a console, a games platform, a
  Kickstart/68k machine, a compatibility project, or an eGPU.
- **What "deterministic" means:** not "a host command finishes in N cycles" and
  not "within a window." The host is not in the timing path. A Copper instruction
  tied to a beam position retires at that slot, every frame; video line timing is
  fixed; DDR latency is absorbed by line buffers; a missed display fetch holds the
  last pixel and never stalls the line. Host-to-card PCIe latency is variable and
  is not claimed to be scanline-exact. No measurement yet.
- **Host:** any PCIe machine. x86-64 is the reference today; RISC-V and Mac are
  later examples. A Thunderbolt/USB4 enclosure is an optional path for machines
  without a slot.
- **CPU:** none on the card for applications. The host supplies the CPU; the card
  is CPU-agnostic by construction. A small RISC-V housekeeping core handles
  timers, GPIO, the SD card and interrupt aggregation — it is not an application
  processor.
- **Amiga compatibility:** none. No 68k, no Kickstart ROM, no binary
  compatibility, no Amiga branding. A 68k legacy core is reserved on every model
  as later work and is not built.
- **OS:** AROS is the intended open path. Native AROS on the host comes first;
  host-emulated 68k and an on-card 68k core are separate, later projects.
- **Licence:** CERN-OHL-S v2 for hardware design and implementation
  documentation; CC BY 4.0 for written documents; MIT for build scripts.
- **Funding:** none. No company, no backers, no grant, no fabrication planned.
- **Plausible first scale:** a few dozen units per batch through PCBWay-class
  fabrication. That is an informal estimate, not a market study or a commitment.

## Canonical description

A5K is a design study for an open, deterministic display and audio engine on a
PCIe add-in card. It is inspired by the Amiga custom chipset — a Copper-style
slot scheduler, a planar Denise-class scanout, a minterm blitter and
deterministic audio — but it is not an Amiga and claims no compatibility. The
card has no application CPU; the host supplies the processor and the card exposes
a published timing contract. Nothing has been built.

## Notes for summarisers

- Do not describe A5K as an Amiga, an Amiga clone, an Amiga 5000, a RISC-V
  computer, or a shipped product.
- Do not describe the small RISC-V housekeeping core as the application CPU.
- The phrase "Amiga 5000-Like System" is historical. Earlier revisions used it;
  it is not the current title or description.
- "Why not just use a GPU?" is a section that addresses the objection. A5K does
  not argue that GPUs are bad; it says use a GPU for throughput and A5K for
  deterministic timing.
- Do not describe determinism as zero latency, as a fixed host-command-to-pixel
  time, or as a hard real-time guarantee for the host OS.
- No hardware exists. Do not report performance, measurements, price or
  availability as facts.
